blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Contextual and unigram surprisal are standard predictors of reading time in computational psycholinguistics. While contextual surprisal is typically derived from neural language models, unigram surprisal is usually obtained from independent corpus counts. Although both quantities are deterministic functionals of a single underlying distribution---capturing conditional and marginal structure respectively---this practice breaks their probabilistic link and may introduce estimation error from the mismatch. We propose three principles for estimating unigram surprisal in psycholinguistic research, including the requirement that both quantities be derived from the same language model. We operationalize this principle by introducing a Monte Carlo estimator of unigram surprisal from a language model, along with a marginalized variant that has lower variance empirically. When unigram surprisal is re-estimated under this unified framework, we find evidence that predictors change in their predictive contribution to reading time. We also confirm prior findings that frequency can be a stronger predictor of processing effort than contextual surprisal under this unified framework.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Human sentence processing is incremental ( Marslen-Wilson, 1975 ; Tanenhaus et al., 1995 ; Rayner and Clifton Jr, 2009 ) and predictive ( Altmann and Kamide, 1999 ; DeLong et al., 2005 ) : comprehenders do not wait until a sentence is complete before interpreting it, but instead build partial representations and continuously generate expectations about upcoming input. Contextual surprisal—the negative log probability of a linguistic unit given its preceding context as derived from language models (LMs)—quantifies the degree to which incoming content aligns with these predictions. Surprisal has been found to robustly predict observed processing effort in humans across paradigms and languages ( Hale, 2001 ; Wilcox et al., 2020 ; Kuribayashi et al., 2022 ; Shain et al., 2024 ) , lending broad empirical support to expectation-based theories of comprehension ( Levy, 2008 ; Kuperberg and Jaeger, 2016 ; Ryskin and Nieuwland, 2023 ) . Separately, the frequency of a unit in a language also shapes how quickly it is processed: more frequent units are recognized faster, independent of their contextual fit ( Hare et al., 1995 ; Bybee, 1998 ; Shain, 2024 ) . This effect is captured by unigram surprisal—the negative log probability of a unit after marginalizing over all contexts. While estimating contextual surprisal has benefited greatly from advances in neural LMs ( Goodkind and Bicknell, 2018 ; Wilcox et al., 2020 ; Oh and Schuler, 2023a ; de Varda and Marelli, 2023 ; Wilcox et al., 2023a ) , unigram surprisal has received comparatively little methodological attention. Typically, it is derived from small-data corpora or lexical databases ( Speer, 2022 ) .

blocks.en: In a sense made specific by Opedal et al. (2024) , contextual surprisal and unigram surprisal are correlated in naturalistic text. That being the case, modern studies on surprisal have controlled for unigram surprisal ( Fernandez Monsalve et al., 2012 ; Smith and Levy, 2013 ; Shain, 2019 ; Wilcox et al., 2023b ; Shain, 2024 ) . However, controlling for unigram surprisal is only meaningful when both estimates come from the same distribution. In the example in Fig. 1 , we calculate contextual surprisal from the language model mGPT ( Shliazhko et al., 2024 ) , while we calculate unigram surprisal with two methods: estimates from the wordfreq package ( Speer, 2022 ) and estimates obtained with a marginalized Monte Carlo (MMC) estimator over the same language model as contextual surprisal. We observe that the pointwise mutual information (PMI) (the difference between unigram and contextual surprisal) is nearly identical for salt and coriander under wordfreq , but diverges substantially under the MMC estimator. This illustrates the estimation error that can arise from a mismatch in unigram and contextual surprisal distributions.

blocks.en:
Motivated by this discrepancy, we put forward a set of three principles to guide approaches to estimating unigram surprisal for research on sentence processing and psycholinguistics more broadly: the best estimate principle, the cognitive plausibility principle, and the consistent distribution principle (see Fig. 2 ; § 5 ).
Though we argue that all three principles should guide unigram surprisal estimations, we note that no existing approach to estimating unigram surprisal satisfies the consistent distribution principle. Such an approach would eliminate the potential for error introduced by mismatched
estimation procedures and allow practitioners to leverage the data scale of large LMs for unigram surprisal estimation.
To that end, we introduce a Monte Carlo estimator that estimates unigram frequency from the same distribution as an LM by sampling strings from the model and calculating a unit’s empirical frequency across these samples. We go on to derive a marginalized variant of the estimator, which we empirically demonstrate to be a more efficient estimator; that is, given the same number of samples, the marginalized variant will obtain lower variance estimates than the naive Monte Carlo estimator.

blocks.en:
In the empirical portion of the article,
we study several predictors of reading times across eleven languages, as in Opedal et al. (2024) , and directly compare models of reading time fit using unigram surprisal values derived from the wordfreq lexical database ( Speer, 2022 ) and values from our MMC estimator.
Like Opedal et al. (2024) , we find that unigram surprisal is a stronger predictor of reading time than contextual surprisal; however, we find that the predictive power of some predictors significantly changes when unigram surprisal is calculated with our MMC estimator.
Though our empirical findings focus specifically on sentence processing, they indicate that the estimation of unigram surprisal should be reconsidered more broadly in computational psycholinguistics.

在文章的经验部分,
我们研究了11种语言的读取时间的几个预测器,如Opedal等人(2024年),并直接比较了使用从Wordfreq lexical数据库(Speer,2022年)得到的unigram surprisal value的读取时间适合的模型,以及我们MMC的估测器得出的数值.
与Opedal等人(2024年)一样,我们发现unigram suprisal比上下文的suprisal更能预测阅读时间;然而,我们发现,当unigrams suprisal用我们的MMC估计器计算时,一些预测器的预测力会发生显著的变化.
虽然我们的经验结论特别侧重于判决处理,但它们表明,在计算心理语言学中,应更广泛地重新考虑对单克合成物的估计。

3 Which Language Model?
blocks.zh: 3 哪一种语言模型?

blocks.en:
Formal theories of language, most notably the generative tradition ( Chomsky, 1957 ; Chomsky, 1965 ) , have historically separated a
speaker’s idealized knowledge of grammatical rules ( competence ) from the
actual, often imperfect, use of language in real-time processing ( performance ).
Probability has found a central role in explaining the latter ( Bod et al., 2003 ; Jurafsky, 2003 ; Chater and Manning, 2006 ; Levy, 2008 ) : under a probabilistic, performance-oriented view
a model of language is then evaluated not by whether it generates the correct set of
grammatical strings, but by how well it mirrors the behavior of human speakers. The
question is thus not whether probability is relevant for modeling linguistic
performance, but what distribution it should approximate. We contrast two
viewpoints on this question, which we refer to as the frequentist and the cognitive
views.

blocks.en: 4 Surprisal Theory
blocks.zh: 4 超常理论

blocks.en:
To study sentence processing during reading, several corpora have been developed in which many participants read the same texts and eye-tracking data are collected while reading ( Kennedy et al., 2003 ; Siegelman et al., 2022 ) .
Eye-tracking studies record participants’ gaze continuously, allowing fixations of varying duration to be mapped directly onto the text ( Rayner, 1998 ) . Although some work has sought to model these fine-grained fixations ( Re et al., 2025 ) , the fixations are generally aggregated to yield a measure of reading time for some unit of interest. The choice of aggregation reflects assumptions about which stage of processing is being targeted ( Rayner, 1998 ; Frank et al., 2013a ; Berzak and Levy, 2023 ) : first fixation duration (the duration of the reader’s first fixation on a unit) is thought to reflect early lexical processing ( Clifton et al., 2007 ) , while gaze duration (cumulative fixation time before first leaving a unit) and total fixation duration (cumulative fixation time including regressions back to the unit) capture progressively later integration processes ( Liversedge et al., 1998 ) .

眼睛跟踪研究不断记录参与者的目光,使不同时期的固定物能够直接被映射到文字上(Rayner,1998年)。 虽然有些工作试图模拟这些精细的固定(Re等,2025年),但一般将这些固定进行汇总,为某些感兴趣的单位提供一定的阅读时间。 汇总的选择反映了对处理阶段目标的假设(Rayner,1998年;Frank等,2013年a;Berzak和Levy,2023年):第一次固定期限(读者第一次固定在一个单位上的时间)被认为反映了早期的语法处理(Clifton等,2007年),而凝视时间(第一次离开一个单位之前的累计固定时间)和总固定期限(累计固定时间,包括返回该单位)则逐渐地捕捉后来的整合过程(Liversedge等,1998年)。

Surprisal theory states that processing difficulty is related to a unit’s negative log probability in a given context ( Hale, 2001 ; Levy, 2008 ; Shain et al., 2024 ) . Psycholinguistic studies test this theory by relating surprisal to
behavioral or neural measures of processing effort such as fixation duration from eye-tracking data ( Wilcox et al., 2023b ) and event-related potentials (ERPs) from electroencephalography ( Frank et al., 2013b ) . LMs play a central role in these studies because they provide estimates of contextual probabilities. 5 Principles of Frequency Estimation
blocks.zh: 5. 频率估计原则

blocks.en: Having discussed which distributions can be modeled to study language and having defined unigram and contextual surprisal, we can now formalize three guiding principles for estimating unigram surprisal and discuss relevant literature around them. The principles are summarized in Fig. 2 .
blocks.zh: 在讨论了哪些分布可以用来研究语言并定义了unigram和上下文外观之后,我们现在可以正式确定估计unigram外观的三项指导原则并讨论围绕这些原则的相关文献。 图2概述了这些原则。

blocks.en:
The first principle adopts an empirical conception of unigram frequency. Under this conception, unigram frequency is treated as a real population quantity: the relative prevalence of a unit in the underlying distribution that generated the corpus. The observed strings are then viewed as samples from that distribution, and estimation amounts to recovering this empirical truth from data. This perspective has two advantages. First, it ties the target quantity to observable language use rather than to an unobserved latent construct. Second, it admits a simple and interpretable estimator: under independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) samples,
unigram probabilities are estimated by normalized token counts, which is equivalent to the maximum-likelihood estimator for a multinomial model; see App. B . As we show in Proposition 2 , because − log -\log is strictly convex, an unbiased estimator of unigram probability does not yield an unbiased estimator of unigram surprisal. Plug-in estimators of related information-theoretic quantities (i.e., entropy) are known to be biased for the same reason ( Miller, 1955 ; Arora et al., 2022 ) . Even for an unbiased unigram probability estimator, the estimated unigram surprisal is biased upward. The bias in surprisal disappears only for a zero-variance unigram probability estimator, motivating lower variance frequency estimators.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en:
The second principle adopts a cognitive conception of unigram frequency. Under this conception, the target is not an empirical population quantity directly given by attested token counts, but a latent property of the expectations in the human mind, as discussed with respect to the cognitive view of the LM ( § 3 ).
The goal is not to simply recover the unigram distribution of the corpus-generating process, but to approximate the distribution that best reflects human baseline expectations over units.
In the past, this has been operationalized as the extent to which frequency values are predictive of human reaction times in lexical decision tasks. This criterion has been studied as an alternative way to validate frequency resources, rather than factors like corpus size ( Keuleers et al., 2010 ; Brysbaert et al., 2011 ) . This has led to findings that texts from the Internet ( Balota et al., 2004 ) or movie and TV subtitles ( New et al., 2007 ) seem to yield more cognitively plausible frequency values than those from edited publications. Importantly, this principle may be at odds with the best estimate principle. Larger LMs, despite achieving lower perplexity, have been found to yield contextual surprisal estimates that are less predictive of processing effort than those of smaller models ( Oh et al., 2022 ; Oh and Schuler, 2023b ) .
One explanation for this is that larger models assign probabilities to very low-frequency units more accurately, but in ways that are less cognitively plausible ( Oh et al., 2024 ) . Similarly, Opedal et al. (2024) argue that medium-sized models may yield contextual surprisal estimates closer to unigram frequency because they are less effective at predicting rare units in context, better matching the balance of contextual and frequency-based information in human processing.
The same issue arises for unigram frequency itself: the statistically best estimate need not be the cognitively most plausible one. Although this question has been studied extensively for contextual surprisal, comparatively little is known about how modeling choices affect the cognitive plausibility of unigram frequency estimates.

第二项原则采用了单相频率的认知概念。 在这个概念下,目标不是经证明的象征性计数直接给出的实证人口数量,而是人脑中期望的潜在属性,正如关于LM认知观点所讨论(§3).
目标不是简单地恢复生成生物体过程的一克分布,而是大致反映最能反映人类对单位的基线期望的分布。
过去,它作为频率值在词汇决定任务中预测人类反应时间的程度而投入使用. 研究了这一标准,将其作为验证频率资源的一种替代方法,而不是实体大小等因素(Keulers等,2010年;Brysbaert等,2011年)。 由此得出的结论是,互联网(Balota等,2004年)或电影和电视字幕(New等,2007年)的文本似乎比编辑过的出版物的文本在认知上的频率值更高。 重要的是,这一原则可能不符合最佳估计原则。 尽管提高了难度,但发现较大的LMs得出了与较小的模型相比对加工努力的预测性较低的上下文外估计值(Oh等人,2022;Oh和Schuler,2023b)。
其中一个解释是,更大的模型更准确地将概率分配给非常低频单位,但其方式在认知上不太合理(Oh等,2024年)。 同样, Opedal等人(2024年)认为,中型模型可能会产生更接近于一克频率的上下文外估计,因为这些模型在上下文中预测稀有单位的效果较低,更能匹配人类处理中上下文信息与频率信息的平衡.
对一克频率本身也会产生同样的问题:统计学上最好的估计不一定是认知上最可信的估计。 虽然这个问题已经为上下文外观进行了广泛的研究,但对于模型选择如何影响单克频率估计的认知可信度,人们所知相对很少.

blocks.en:
The third principle is that contextual and unigram surprisal should be derived from the same distribution. Although the literature often
estimates them from different sources,
the two quantities are not independent: both are functionals of a single distribution over linguistic sequences. Contextual surprisal reflects its conditional structure, while unigram surprisal reflects the marginal distribution it induces over units. Under a shared distribution, this relationship holds by construction. Under heterogeneous estimation, it does not: the two predictors then summarize different probabilistic models rather than a single generative system. Our unified estimation framework restores this coherence by deriving both quantities from the same LM. The consistent distribution principle has been observed before, though it has primarily been addressed by changing the corpora used to calculate unigram frequency. For example, Shain (2024) calculate contextual surprisal with GPT-2. To calculate unigram surprisal, Shain use a corpus that was specifically chosen to approximate the model’s training distribution in an effort to minimize effects from this mismatch. Likewise, in their assessment of surprisal as a measure of metaphor novelty, Momen and Zarrieß (2026) compare unigram surprisals from wordfreq ( Speer, 2022 ) to those calculated over the training data of the LMs they use to obtain contextual surprisal.

Wherever
PMI or unigram surprisal appear in our models, we report results using both the original wordfreq estimates ( Speer, 2022 ) and each of our approaches to estimating unigram surprisal from mGPT. We model reading times using generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs), which differ from linear models by allowing predictors to enter through smooth, nonparametric functions rather than fixed linear coefficients. Our dependent variable is gaze duration. We fit five GAMMs with smooth terms for
(i) unigram surprisal, (ii) contextual surprisal, (iii) PMI,
(iv) contextual surprisal and unigram surprisal, and
(v) PMI and unigram surprisal, each with a single spillover term per predictor and random effect smooths for participant and trial.
Model fit is assessed via delta log-likelihood ( Δ LL {{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\Delta_{\text{LL}}}} ),
defined as the difference in per-unit log-likelihood between a candidate model
and a baseline with only random effects.
Predictions are obtained via 10-fold cross-validation;
positive values indicate that the candidate model assigns higher likelihood to the observed reading times than this baseline. To assess whether the MMC estimators
yield a different quality of fit than corpus-based unigram surprisals, we compare Δ LL {{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\Delta_{\text{LL}}}} values between the two frequency conditions at the unit level
using paired permutation tests, with p p -values
corrected for multiple comparisons using the Holm–Bonferroni procedure. We discuss MECO and the covered languages, preprocessing, model specification, and evaluation details in App. F .

blocks.en: We also investigate the coverage of the naive Monte Carlo estimate, i.e., for how many unigrams in MECO it successfully obtains estimates. Obtaining an estimate with the Naive Monte Carlo estimator requires the unigram to occur in the sample pool, which is not guaranteed. Across a range of mGPT sample sizes from N = 10 2 N=10^{2} to N = 10 7 N=10^{7} , we find that NMC never successfully obtains estimates for 100% of the types in the MECO corpus for any of the 11 languages tested here, and even obtains less than 50% coverage for Finnish types in sample pools of 10 7 10^{7} strings (see App. E ).

blocks.en: Importantly, our coverage experiment indicates that sampled text from mGPT is skewed toward Hebrew, Greek, and Russian. Thus, while the MMC estimator does not have the same coverage problems as the NMC estimator, the sampled contexts used for estimates may not be informative (i.e., because they are from different languages). To better adapt our estimator for use with multilingual language models, we introduce priority-MMC, which draws samples from a large pool with language-specific strata (see App. I for details).
blocks.zh: 重要的是,我们的报道实验表明,MGPT的样本文本向希伯来语、希腊语和俄语倾斜。 因此,虽然MMC估计仪的覆盖范围问题与NMC估计仪不同,但用于估计的抽样背景可能不具有信息性(即因为它们来自不同的语言)。 为了更好地调整我们的估算器,使之与多语种语言模型相适应,我们引入了优先MMC,它从一个具有语言特殊层次的大集合中取出样本(详见App.I).

blocks.en: 8.2 Downstream Impact of Marginalizing
blocks.zh: 8.2 边缘化的下游影响

blocks.en: We now focus on models of gaze duration fit with various unigram estimates: corpus-based estimates from wordfreq ( Speer, 2022 ) , NMC estimates, MMC estimates and their canonical-only approximations (MMC and MMC Approx.), and priority-MMC estimates and their canonical-only approximations (Priority MMC and Priority MMC Approx.). We present bootstrapped distributions of item-level Δ LL {{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\Delta_{\text{LL}}}} for GAMMs modeling gaze duration in Fig. 3 . Across all MMC variants, we consistently observe a significant increase in Δ LL {{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\Delta_{\text{LL}}}} for GAMMs fit with PMI calculated with MMC unigram surprisals, relative to GAMMs fit with PMI calculated with wordfreq unigram surprisals. As in prior work ( Opedal et al., 2024 ; Heilbron et al., 2023 ) , we find that unigram surprisal is a stronger predictor of reading times than contextual surprisal; our results confirm this finding in an environment where both values come from the same underlying distribution. We note that because of relatively poor coverage (even at high sample sizes) for rarer words, more samples are excluded from the NMC models, meaning the results are likely less robust than those from the various MMC estimators. Though the MMC and priority MMC estimators properly account for non-canonical tokenizations, our findings indicate that approximations over only canonical samples yield similar results with higher coverage and less computational cost. The results highlight that principled approaches to estimating unigram surprisal have a downstream impact.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 9 结论

blocks.en:
This paper highlights an understudied matter in surprisal theory literature—while much attention has been given to how we estimate contextual surprisal, little research has focused on how we estimate unigram surprisal. We propose three principles to guide this estimation and introduce a Monte Carlo estimator of unigram surprisal from a language model, along with several marginalized variants. By deriving both surprisal quantities from the same model, differences in predictive power can be attributed to modeling decisions rather than mismatched estimation procedures.
Our experiments show that the choice of unigram surprisal estimator has empirical consequences, and we provide further support that contextual surprisal is a weaker predictor of reading times than unigram surprisal in modeling reading time. We hope this encourages future work on what modeling decisions result in cognitively plausible unigram surprisal estimations and a more careful consideration of the role of frequency in computational psycholinguistics.

本文强调了在超额理论文献中一个研究不足的问题——虽然我们非常关注我们如何估计背景超额,但很少研究我们如何估计unigram超额。 我们提出了指导这一估计的三项原则,并从语言模型中引入了单一语种的Monte Carlo估算法,以及一些边缘化的变体。 通过从同一种模型中推导出两种超额量,预测力的差异可以归因于建模决定,而不是不匹配的估计程序.
我们的实验表明,独角兽实验(unigram suprisal estimator)的选择会产生经验性后果,我们提供进一步的支持,即上下文外观是比独角兽实验(unigram suprisal)在模拟阅读时间时更弱的阅读时间预测. 我们希望这能鼓励今后就模拟决定产生何种认知上可信的单格合成估计以及更仔细地考虑频率在计算心理语言学中的作用而开展工作。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Though we argue that our principles for estimating unigram surprisal are applicable to computational psycholinguistics as a whole, we limit our analyses to sentence processing. We find that the procedure for estimating unigram surprisal has an empirical impact when it comes to modeling reading times, but the claim warrants further investigation in other lines of computational psycholinguistics research, e.g., in modeling speech segmentation during language acquisition or acceptability judgment experiments.
blocks.zh: 虽然我们主张我们估算单格超额的原则适用于计算心理语言学整体,但我们的分析仅限于判决处理. 我们发现,在模拟阅读时间时,估计unigram suprisal的程序具有经验影响,但这一主张值得在计算心理语言学研究的其他行中作进一步调查,例如,在语言获取或可接受性判断实验中模拟语音分化.

blocks.en: In general, estimating unigram surprisal from a language model is computationally expensive compared to using lexical databases or corpus counts, particularly for the marginalized estimators we present. Because of their lower variance, the marginalized variants of our estimator also address this limitation of our method to some extent: relatively few samples are required to obtain stable estimates compared to the Naive Monte Carlo estimator. Still, computational resources limited our sample size and the maximum string length of the strings sampled from mGPT.
blocks.zh: 一般而言,与使用词汇数据库或实体计算相比,从语言模型中估算unigram surprisal在计算上是昂贵的,特别是对于我们所介绍的被边缘化的估算者而言。 由于差异较小,我们的估算器的边缘变量也在一定程度上解决了我们方法的这一局限性:与Naive Monte Carlo估算器相比,获得稳定估算所需的样本较少。 尽管如此,计算资源还是限制了我们的样本大小和从mGPT所取样本的字符串的最大长度.

blocks.en: We also study a limited scope of units. Our implementation of the unit parser matches whitespace-initial token spans ( App. C ), which is adequate for the whitespace-delimited orthographies studied here but not in general. Whether the impact of the specific estimator used varies with units of interest (for example, characters or the contextually defined words studied in Kiegeland et al. (2026) ) remains an open question.
blocks.zh: 我们还研究有限的单位范围。 我们执行的单元解析器符合白空-初始符号跨度(App. C),适合在此所研究的白空-受限的正字形,但一般不在此列. 使用的具体估算符的影响是否因感兴趣的单位而异(例如:字符或基格兰等人(2026年)所研究的上下文定义的单词),仍然是一个尚未解决的问题.

blocks.en: Ethical Concerns

blocks.en: This study uses eye-tracking data from human participants. Because the dataset has already been published ( Siegelman et al., 2022 ) , we foresee no new ethical concerns from the contributions made in this paper.

blocks.en: Our results demonstrate that for unigrams of token length T = 1 T=1 , both estimators incur similar costs, which are mainly from the generation of N = 500 N=500 strings. For multi-token unigrams, however, the MMC estimator scales with token count while times for the NMC estimator are stable. This is a consequence of our estimation of the joint probability of all the tokens in multi-token unigrams, which requires T − 1 T-1 additional rounds of batched forward passes over all positions in the sampled contexts. Still, this cost is paid only once per unit in the dataset, and the faster NMC estimates for multi-token words come at the cost of higher variance estimates relative to the MMC estimator (see Tab. 1 and Fig. 4 ).

blocks.en: All reading time data used in our models is obtained from the L1 portion of the MECO corpus ( Siegelman et al., 2022 ) . Our selection of the eleven languages used here represents the overlap between languages in MECO and those supported by the LM used in our experiments, mGPT. In preprocessing, we remove words skipped by participants and obtain first fixation duration (i.e., the length of the participant’s first fixation on a word), gaze duration (the total time a participant fixates on a word before leaving it the first time) and the total fixation duration (the total time a participant fixates on a word regardless of whether they left the word and came back to it later). In their description of MECO, Siegelman et al. (2022) report on their procedure for aligning fixations to words and filtering data due to poor eye-tracker calibration. Tables throughout the section give the fold sizes in the 10-fold cross-validation used for GAMM evaluation (see § 7 ), which differ between estimators due to differences in coverage.
blocks.zh: 我们模型中使用的所有读取时间数据均取自MECO的L1部分(Siegelman等,2022年)。 我们选择这里使用的十一种语言,代表了MECO语言与我们实验中使用的LM支持的语言mGPT的重叠. 在预处理中,我们删除参与者跳过的单词,并获得第一次固定时间(即参与者第一次固定在单词上的长度),凝视时间(参与者在第一次离开之前固定在单词上的总时间)和总固定时间(参与者无论是否离开单词而返回单词上的总时间)。 在对MECO的描述中,Siegelman等人(2022年)报告了由于眼睛跟踪器校正不当而使其固定值与单词一致并过滤数据的程序. 全节的表格给出了用于GAMM评价的10倍交叉验证中的折叠大小(见第7节),由于覆盖范围不同,估计器之间有差异.

blocks.en: Table 13 shows the sampling parameters of both variants. We allocated the per-unit budget k k in three steps: we divide a fixed share among the strata of the languages in which the unit occurs, half of it going to a generic Latin stratum for languages written in Latin script. Every stratum that carries mass receives a floor of 64 64 boundaries, the rest is divided in proportion to each stratum’s share of the unit’s first-token mass, capped at the stratum’s total from the first two steps. Any residue is divided by mass alone, such that the full budget is spent whenever the stored cells can serve it.
